fullPassage:
The Magic of Morning Pages

Welcome to my channel Good Habits! This is Regan, your podcast host. Today, I'm going to talk about a way of starting the day that many people, including me, find enormously useful. It's a kind of journaling called "the morning pages." There is no age at which it is too late to form this habit. I started eight years ago as a high school student, and that's why today's episode is especially for my teenage subscribers.

The morning pages are three pages of "free writing," ideally done first thing in the morning. The concept is simple. Get up every morning, pick up a pen and a notebook, and write whatever crosses your mind until you have filled three pages. The technique was originally developed to help writers and artists overcome a loss of creativity, but anybody can use it to create a better life.

There is no right or wrong way to write your morning pages, but there are two rules. First, don't judge your writing as good or bad. These pages are meant to be a "brain cleansing," so don't worry about writing correctly. Second, keep your writing completely private. It is important for you to write freely and honestly. You're even advised not to read your writing yourself for weeks.

Now, let me share the experiences of some people I interviewed. David, a chef and kitchen manager, who has been writing morning pages for two years, says:

My job tends to be very stressful. When I started writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of complaints about my hard life. Later, I began to ask questions, like "What would make my life easier today?" "How can I improve my recipes?" Sometimes, I keep asking questions until I reach a sort of "click moment." It feels like a door opening to great ideas. Nowadays, I feel less stressed, enjoy my job more, and am more productive.

Now, let's listen to Yuna, a high school junior:

When I started this exercise last year, I simply wrote random thoughts like this:
I'm sleepy. A slight headache's starting.
I need to finish the math assignment today …
I don't know what more to write now.

But soon I found I had deeper and deeper thoughts. Now, I normally start by writing about today's tasks or worries. After that, I write about my dreams and how to move towards them. I often come up with great plans and a clear sense of purpose to start the day. Most importantly, I'm much happier than before.

I can totally relate to these two people because their experiences are similar to mine. Like Yuna, I started this journaling during my first year of high school. At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and unsure about the future, and it wasn't easy for me to concentrate. When I first tried writing three daily pages, I didn't expect to stick to it. But I did, and it changed my life!

Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning helped relieve my emotional tension. I gained more inner peace, which improved my schoolwork performance. Like David, I asked many questions, for instance, "Why was I so angry yesterday?" "Why are things less fun these days?" Then, I started raising more challenging ones: "What could make me happier right now?" "What is my ideal future? Can I reach it? How?"

Answering these questions showed me what kind of person I was and what my needs, values, passions, and talents were. More importantly, I came to know what I truly wanted! I remembered my childhood dreams of being a writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, vague ideas became clear plans. Years later, here I am, a successful podcaster and vlogger! I've also published a book and a music album. My morning pages, which I still write every day, have given me the drive and ideas to achieve these aims.

Dear subscribers, will you try writing your morning pages, too? You never know what creative energy or ideas you have until you start exploring. Don't be a perfectionist, though. If you miss a few days, simply open your notebook and start again! The ultimate aim is to improve your mental health and help you lead a happier, more creative life.

questions.passage: Today, I'm going to talk about a way of starting the day that many people, including me, find (A)[enormously / slightly] useful. It's a kind of journaling called "the morning pages." There is no age at which it is too late to form this habit. I started eight years ago as a high school student, and that's why today's episode is (B)[especially / barely] for my teenage (C)[subscribers / competitors].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 많은 사람들이 엄청나게(enormously) 유용하다고 생각하는 방법이고, 특히(especially) 십대 구독자(subscribers)를 위한 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① enormously — especially — subscribers: 원문 그대로
❌ ② slightly(약간): enormously(엄청나게)의 반의어
❌ ③ barely(간신히): especially(특히)의 반의어
❌ ④ 세 단어 모두 원문과 반대
det.tip: enormously(엄청나게) = immensely, hugely. subscriber(구독자) ↔ competitor(경쟁자)

questions.passage: The technique was originally developed to help writers and artists (A)[overcome / maintain] a loss of creativity, but anybody can use it to create a better life. There is no right or wrong way to write your morning pages, but there are two rules. First, don't (B)[judge / praise] your writing as good or bad. These pages are meant to be a "brain cleansing," so don't worry about writing (C)[correctly / creatively].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이 기법은 원래 작가와 예술가들이 창조력 상실을 극복하도록(overcome) 돕기 위해 개발됐다. 글을 좋다 나쁘다 판단하지(judge) 마라. 올바르게(correctly) 쓰는 것에 대해 걱정하지 마라.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ overcome — judge — correctly: 원문 일치
❌ ① maintain(유지하다): overcome(극복하다)의 반의어
❌ ② praise(칭찬하다): judge(판단하다)와 반대
❌ ③ 모두 원문과 다름
det.tip: overcome(극복하다) ↔ maintain(유지하다). judge(판단하다): 비판적 평가를 뜻함

questions.passage: Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning helped relieve my emotional (A)[tension / satisfaction]. I gained more inner peace, which improved my schoolwork performance. Like David, I asked many questions, for instance, "Why was I so angry yesterday?" Then, I started raising more (B)[challenging / effortless] ones. Answering these questions showed me what kind of person I was and what my needs, values, (C)[passions / obligations], and talents were.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 감정을 종이에 풀어놓는 것이 정서적 긴장(tension)을 완화하는 데 도움이 됐다. 더 도전적인(challenging) 질문들을 시작했다. 나의 필요, 가치, 열정(passions), 재능이 무엇인지 알게 되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ tension — challenging — passions: 원문 일치
❌ ① satisfaction(만족): tension(긴장)의 반의어
❌ ② effortless(수월한): challenging(도전적인)의 반의어
❌ ④ 모두 원문과 반대
det.tip: tension(긴장) ↔ satisfaction(만족). passion(열정) ↔ obligation(의무)

questions.passage: My job tends to be very ①<u>stressful</u>. When I started writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of ②<u>complaints</u> about my hard life. Later, I began to ask questions, like "What would make my life easier today?" Sometimes, I keep asking questions until I reach a sort of "click moment." It feels like a door ③<u>opening</u> to great ideas. Nowadays, I feel less stressed, enjoy my job more, and am more ④<u>lazy</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ lazy(게으른)는 원문 productive(생산적인)의 반의어. 요즘 스트레스도 덜 받고 일도 더 즐기고 더 생산적이다(productive).
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ lazy: 원문은 productive(생산적인). 긍정적 맥락에 lazy(게으른)는 부적절
❌ ① stressful(스트레스가 많은): 원문 그대로
❌ ② complaints(불평): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ opening(열리는): 원문 그대로
det.tip: productive(생산적인) ↔ lazy(게으른). 결과를 나타내는 긍정 맥락 파악 중요

questions.passage: When I started this exercise last year, I simply wrote ①<u>random</u> thoughts. But soon I found I had deeper and deeper thoughts. Now, I normally start by writing about today's tasks or ②<u>worries</u>. After that, I write about my dreams and how to move towards them. I often come up with great plans and a clear sense of ③<u>confusion</u> to start the day. Most importantly, I'm much ④<u>happier</u> than before.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ confusion(혼란)은 원문 purpose(목적의식)의 반의어. 멋진 계획들과 하루를 시작할 뚜렷한 목적의식(purpose)을 얻는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ③ confusion: 원문은 purpose(목적의식). 꿈을 향해 나아가는 긍정 맥락에 confusion(혼란)은 부적절
❌ ① random(마구잡이): 원문 그대로
❌ ② worries(걱정): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ happier(더 행복한): 원문 그대로
det.tip: a clear sense of purpose = 뚜렷한 목적의식. purpose(목적) ↔ confusion(혼란)

questions.passage: Like Yuna, I started this journaling during my first year of high school. At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and ①<u>unsure</u> about the future, and it wasn't easy for me to ②<u>concentrate</u>. When I first tried writing three daily pages, I didn't expect to stick to it. But I did, and it changed my life! Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning helped ③<u>intensify</u> my emotional tension. I gained more inner peace, which ④<u>improved</u> my schoolwork performance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ intensify(강화하다)는 원문 relieve(완화하다)의 반의어. 감정을 종이에 풀어놓는 것이 정서적 긴장을 완화하는(relieve) 데 도움이 됐다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ③ intensify: 원문은 relieve(완화하다). 감정 해소 → 긴장 '완화'가 자연스러움
❌ ① unsure(확신 없는): 원문 그대로
❌ ② concentrate(집중하다): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ improved(향상시켰다): 원문 그대로
det.tip: relieve(완화하다) ↔ intensify(강화하다). emotional tension = 정서적 긴장

questions.passage: The morning pages are three pages of "free writing," ideally done first thing in the morning. The concept is simple. Get up every morning, pick up a pen and a notebook, and write whatever crosses your mind until you have filled three pages. The technique was originally developed to help writers and artists overcome a loss of __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 기법은 원래 작가와 예술가들이 창조력(creativity) 상실을 극복하도록 돕기 위해 개발됐다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② creativity: 원문 a loss of creativity 그대로
❌ ① productivity(생산성): 작가/예술가 맥락에 부적합
❌ ③ popularity(인기): 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ responsibility(책임감): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: creativity(창조력) — 작가와 예술가에게 핵심 자질. overcome a loss of ~ = ~의 상실을 극복하다

questions.passage: Like Yuna, I started this journaling during my first year of high school. At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and unsure about the future, and it wasn't easy for me to concentrate. When I first tried writing three daily pages, I didn't expect to stick to it. But I did, and it changed my life! Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning helped relieve my emotional __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 감정을 종이에 풀어놓는 것이 정서적 긴장(tension)을 완화하는 데 도움이 됐다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① tension: 원문 emotional tension 그대로. relieve(완화)의 대상
❌ ② freedom(자유): relieve freedom은 의미상 부자연스러움
❌ ③ curiosity(호기심): 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ confidence(자신감): relieve confidence는 부적절
det.tip: emotional tension = 정서적 긴장. relieve tension = 긴장을 완화하다

questions.passage: Answering these questions showed me what kind of person I was and what my needs, values, passions, and talents were. More importantly, I came to know what I truly wanted! I remembered my childhood dreams of being a writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, __________ ideas became clear plans. Years later, here I am, a successful podcaster and vlogger!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 막연한(vague) 아이디어들이 차츰 명확한 계획이 되어갔다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ vague: 원문 vague ideas became clear plans. 막연한 → 명확한 대비
❌ ① precise(정밀한): clear plans와 의미가 겹쳐 대비 구조가 성립 안 됨
❌ ② brilliant(훌륭한): 대비 구조에 맞지 않음
❌ ④ ambitious(야심찬): 문맥상 '야심찬 아이디어가 명확한 계획이 되었다'는 어색
det.tip: vague(막연한) ↔ clear(명확한). 대비 구조를 통해 빈칸 추론 가능

questions.passage: My job tends to be very stressful. When I started writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of complaints about my hard life. Later, I began to ask questions. Nowadays, I feel less stressed, enjoy my job more, and am more <u>productive</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 productive의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: productive = 생산적인, efficient = 효율적인 (동의어)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ efficient(효율적인): productive(생산적인)의 동의어
❌ ① exhausted(지친): 반의어
❌ ② anxious(불안한): 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ distracted(산만한): productive의 반의어
det.tip: productive(생산적인) = efficient(효율적인). 반의어: unproductive, idle

questions.passage: There is no right or wrong way to write your morning pages, but there are two rules. First, don't judge your writing as good or bad. These pages are meant to be a "brain cleansing," so don't worry about writing correctly. Second, keep your writing completely <u>private</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 private의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: private = 비공개의, confidential = 비밀의 (동의어)
det.analysis:
✅ ② confidential(비밀의): private(비공개의)의 동의어
❌ ① public(공개적인): private의 반의어
❌ ③ official(공식적인): 관련 없음
❌ ④ popular(인기 있는): 관련 없음
det.tip: private(비공개의) = confidential(비밀의) = secret. 반의어: public(공개적인)

questions.passage: I can totally relate to these two people because their experiences are similar to mine. Like Yuna, I started this journaling during my first year of high school. At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and unsure about the future, and it wasn't easy for me to <u>concentrate</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 concentrate의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: concentrate = 집중하다, focus = 집중하다 (동의어)
det.analysis:
✅ ① focus(집중하다): concentrate(집중하다)의 동의어
❌ ② relax(쉬다): 집중과 반대
❌ ③ complain(불평하다): 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ wander(헤매다): concentrate의 반의어
det.tip: concentrate(집중하다) = focus. 반의어: wander, lose focus

questions.passage: Dear subscribers, will you try writing your morning pages, too? You never know what creative energy or ideas you have until you start exploring. Don't be a <u>perfectionist</u>, though. If you miss a few days, simply open your notebook and start again!
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 perfectionist의 의미와 가장 반대되는 것은?

det.korean: perfectionist = 완벽주의자, easygoing person = 느긋한 사람 (반의어)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ easygoing person(느긋한 사람): perfectionist(완벽주의자)의 반의어
❌ ① idealist(이상주의자): 유사한 뉘앙스
❌ ② specialist(전문가): 관련 없음
❌ ③ activist(활동가): 관련 없음
det.tip: perfectionist(완벽주의자): 모든 것을 완벽하게 하려는 사람 ↔ easygoing(느긋한)

questions.passage: Answering these questions showed me what kind of person I was and what my needs, values, passions, and talents were. More importantly, I came to know what I truly wanted! I remembered my childhood dreams. Gradually, <u>vague</u> ideas became clear plans.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 vague의 의미와 가장 반대되는 것은?

det.korean: vague = 막연한, specific = 구체적인 (반의어)
det.analysis:
✅ ② specific(구체적인): vague(막연한)의 반의어
❌ ① abstract(추상적인): vague와 유사어
❌ ③ uncertain(불확실한): vague와 유사어
❌ ④ ambiguous(모호한): vague와 유사어
det.tip: vague(막연한) = abstract = uncertain ↔ specific(구체적인) = clear = definite. 오답이 모두 유사어라 혼동 주의

questions.passage:
(A) The technique was originally developed to help writers and artists overcome a loss of creativity, but anybody can use it to create a better <u>life</u>.
(B) My job tends to be very stressful. When I started writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of complaints about my hard <u>life</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 life가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) create a better life = 더 나은 삶(인생)을 만들다 — 인생 전체를 의미 (B) complaints about my hard life = 힘든 생활(일상)에 대한 불평 — 일상적 생활을 의미
det.analysis:
✅ ④ (A) 삶(인생) – (B) 생활(일상): (A)는 better life로 인생 전체, (B)는 hard life로 힘든 일상
❌ ① 생명: life에 생명 뜻이 있지만 이 문맥에는 부적합
❌ ② 둘 다 생활: (A)는 인생 전체적 의미
❌ ③ (A)가 생명: 문맥상 부적합
det.tip: life의 다의어: 생명(life and death), 삶/인생(lead a better life), 생활(daily life)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to continue doing something even though it is difficult"

det.korean: "어렵더라도 계속하다" = stick to(~를 고수하다/계속하다)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ stick to: 어렵더라도 계속하다. 본문에서 'I didn't expect to stick to it'
❌ ① overcome(극복하다): 어려움을 이겨내다
❌ ② concentrate(집중하다): 주의를 기울이다
❌ ④ relieve(완화하다): 줄이다
det.tip: stick to = ~을 고수하다, 계속하다. I stuck to the plan = 계획을 고수했다

questions.passage: These pages are meant to be a "brain cleansing," so don't worry about writing correctly. Second, keep your writing completely private. It is important for you to write freely and __________. (honest) You're even advised not to read your writing yourself for weeks.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 자유롭고 솔직하게(honestly) 쓰는 것이 중요하다.
det.analysis: ✅ honestly: 부사 freely와 병렬 → and 뒤에도 부사 형태 필요. honest(형용사) → honestly(부사)
det.tip: and로 연결된 병렬구조: freely and honestly. 형용사 → 부사: -ly 추가

questions.passage: I remembered my childhood dreams of being a writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, vague ideas became clear plans. Years later, here I am, a __________ podcaster and vlogger! (success)
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 몇 년 후 나는 성공적인(successful) 팟캐스터이자 브이로거로서 여기에 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ successful: 명사 podcaster를 수식하는 형용사 필요. success(명사) → successful(형용사)
det.tip: success(명사) → successful(형용사) → successfully(부사). 명사 앞 수식어 = 형용사

questions.passage: Now, let me share the experiences of some people I interviewed. David, a chef and kitchen manager, who has been writing morning pages for two years, says: My job tends to be very stressful. When I started writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of complaints about my hard life. Later, I began to ask questions. Sometimes, I keep asking questions until I reach a sort of "__________".
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 질문을 계속하다 보면 일종의 '클릭 순간(click moment)'에 도달한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② click moment: 원문 그대로. 아이디어가 딱 맞아떨어지는 순간
❌ ① breaking point(한계점): 부정적 뉘앙스
❌ ③ turning point(전환점): 유사하지만 원문과 다름
❌ ④ final answer(최종 답): 문맥과 다름
det.tip: click moment = 아이디어가 딱 맞아떨어지는 순간. "It feels like a door opening to great ideas."

questions.passage: Dear subscribers, will you try writing your morning pages, too? You never know what creative energy or ideas you have until you start exploring. Don't be a perfectionist, though. If you miss a few days, simply open your notebook and start again! The ultimate aim is to improve your __________ and help you lead a happier, more creative life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 궁극적인 목표는 정신 건강(mental health)을 개선하고 더 행복하고 창조적인 삶을 영위하는 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ mental health: 원문 그대로. 모닝페이지의 궁극적 목표
❌ ① social status(사회적 지위): 문맥과 무관
❌ ② academic grades(학업 성적): 부분적이지만 궁극적 목표가 아님
❌ ③ physical fitness(체력): 정신 건강이 아닌 신체 건강
det.tip: mental health = 정신 건강. The ultimate aim = 궁극적인 목표
